metadata.title: Receipted Comparator Checks of Two Lean Proofs on Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function, with Formalizations of the Bohr–Landau Theorem and a Zero-Density Estimate
metadata.description:
This paper reports eleven runs of Comparator, the Lean FRO's proof judge, under a pinned, sandboxed protocol, each with a published receipt. Two runs repeat checks of public Lean 4 proofs on zeros of the Riemann zeta function: OpenAI's theorem that zeta has no zeros with real part above 7/8, and zeta23, Anthropic's formalization of Alpöge and Furman's theorem that more than two thirds of the zeros are simple and on the critical line (as judged: for every ε > 0, a proportion at least 2/3 − ε at all large heights). Both ended in PASS: the pinned proof was accepted by the Lean kernel (and NanoDa for zeta23) against the pinned statement file, using only the axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. Nine further accepted runs judge Lean files added to the verified trees: the author's library MNF.RH, and a layer formalizing the Bohr–Landau theorem, a zero-density estimate with a power saving weaker than Carlson's, a bound for the zeros' total displacement from the critical line that is far weaker than Littlewood's and Selberg's, two equivalences that restate, and do not prove, the Riemann hypothesis with simplicity and a zero-free-strip hypothesis of the author's library, and the absence of real zeros of zeta in (0,1). The analytic results are classical or weaker than classical ones; Lean zero-density estimates with stronger exponents, which imply the one-sided Bohr–Landau bound, were registered earlier by others, and earlier Lean proofs of the absence of real zeros exist. Nothing here proves, or is evidence for, the Riemann hypothesis, the simplicity of the zeros, or a zero-free strip next to the critical line. The layer's Lean files (apart from four supporting files, which the author supplied), parts of MNF.RH, the scripts and the text of the paper were produced with Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent, under the direction of the author, who conceived the MNF framework, set the goals, operated every run and is responsible for the claims.

Files: the paper (PDF), and a snapshot of the public record github.com/Joeyxyxyz/qrh-comparator-receipts (the kit, nine add-ons, eleven receipt bundles, the register DEPOSIT_MAP.md, the verifier verify_deposit.sh, unpacked sources, working notes, and the paper's source and review record).
metadata.notes: Licenses: the text of the paper is under CC BY 4.0; the files of the record (scripts, documents, the author's Lean files, the receipts) are under the Apache License 2.0 (LICENSE, NOTICE in the snapshot). The theorems under test belong to OpenAI and to Anthropic and Alpöge-Furman and are credited as such; the runs repeat checks and are not first verifications. Use of AI tools is stated in the paper's section 'Authorship and use of AI tools'. This file is a helper for filling the Zenodo form by hand; it replaces the metadata drafted on 2026-10-29 for a dataset deposit of runs 1 to 6.
